# Preset Intake Manifest

Staging area for the self-hosted gatedDAW factory preset catalog (see `docs/self-hosted-roadmap.md`,
"Add local preset packs"). Generated by `scripts/generate-presets.mjs`, run with no arguments so it
wrote directly into this directory (its default root). Nine `.odp` files plus `index.json` (a flat
array of `PresetMeta` entries, matching the shape `presets/index.json` needs — same convention
`scripts/mirror-factory-assets.mjs` already reads: `presets/<uuid>.odp` + a flat metadata array,
not the nested folder-tree shape soundfonts/samples catalogs use).

**Total: 9 presets, 19,970 bytes across the `.odp` files (1,941–2,697 bytes each) + a 2,712-byte
`index.json`.** (Slightly larger than the superseded draft — the real generated box classes carry a
few more default/mandatory fields per box than the hand-transcribed version assumed.)

## How these were built

Each `.odp` is `PresetHeader.MAGIC_HEADER_OPEN` ("OPRE") + format version (1) + a serialized
`BoxGraph`, constructed the same way `PresetEncoder.encode`/`encodeEffects` build one: a skeleton
(`GrooveShuffleBox`, `RootBox`, the primary Output `AudioBusBox`/`AudioUnitBox`, `TimelineBox` +
tempo-track `ValueEventCollectionBox`) plus either a real instrument `AudioUnitBox` (for
`instrument`/`audio-unit` presets) or a synthetic wrapper `AudioUnitBox` hosting a
`NoopInstrumentBox` (for `audio-effect-chain` presets), with the actual devices hosted on its
`audioEffects`/`input` field. Field keys, types, and default values were transcribed directly from
`packages/studio/forge-boxes/src/schema/**` (the real schema source), and the encoder builds each
box graph using the real field/pointer wiring rules — a device's own default parameter values are
used everywhere except where a preset's character required a deliberate, noted deviation.

**Verification note (superseded, kept for history):** an earlier pass in this same session
generated a first draft using a hand-rolled re-implementation of the box/field wiring (see git
history of this file), because the Windows dev checkout this repo normally lives on (`T:\`) turned
out to be formatted **exFAT**, which cannot create the NTFS junctions/symlinks `npm install` needs
to link the `@opendaw/*` workspace packages — so no real build was possible there at all, not even
`node_modules/.bin` tooling. That draft was explicitly flagged as unverified against the real
engine and has since been replaced.

**Real verification (current):** the repo was mirrored to an NTFS drive (`C:\dev\OpenDAW`), where
`npm install` and `npx turbo build --filter=@opendaw/studio-adapters...` succeeded cleanly,
producing real `dist/` output for every dependency, including running the actual `box-forge`
codegen (`packages/studio/forge-boxes`) that generates `packages/studio/boxes/src/*.ts` — the
literal generated device classes (`CompressorDeviceBox`, `SoundfontDeviceBox`, etc.), not a
transcription of them. `scripts/generate-presets.mjs` was rewritten to import and call those real
classes plus the real `ProjectSkeleton`/`AudioUnitFactory`/`PresetEncoder`/`PresetHeader` from
`@opendaw/studio-adapters` directly (run via `npx tsx`, needed only because the compiled output's
extensionless relative imports don't resolve under plain Node's strict ESM resolver — the same
constraint the repo's own `forge.ts` codegen step already works around the same way). All 9 presets
were then round-tripped through the real `PresetDecoder` (`PresetDecoder.decode` for
instrument/rack presets, `PresetDecoder.insertEffectChain` for chain presets — the same calls
`PresetEncoder.composite.test.ts`'s real, passing vitest suite uses) into a fresh target
`ProjectSkeleton`, confirming every mandatory pointer resolves and, for the three asset-referencing
presets, that `Convolver.file`/`Soundfont.file` resolve to an `AudioFileBox`/`SoundfontFileBox`
carrying the expected precomputed UUID and file name. The soundfont `preset-index` values (0 for
Clean Piano, 20 for Orchestral Harp) were also independently re-confirmed by loading both `.sf2`
files with the same `soundfont2` npm package the real engine uses
(`packages/studio/core-wasm/src/soundfont-simplify.ts`) and checking the **array index** of the
intended patch in `sf2.presets` — the field is an ordinal position in that array, not a
bank/program-encoded number, which the first draft got right by an unverified guess; this pass
confirmed it wasn't luck. The UUIDs, byte sizes, and filenames below are this real run's actual
output, written directly into this directory.

Every other field left at the Vaporisateur instrument-factory defaults (same baseline `InstrumentFactories.Vaporisateur` itself uses). |
| Orchestral Sketch (Harp) | instrument | Soundfont (FreePats GM Orchestral) | **Asset dependency**, see below. Deliberately scoped down — see "Skipped/scoped-down". `preset-index` 20 = "Orchestral Harp" (GM bank 0 / program 46), confirmed the same way as Clean Piano. |

## Asset dependencies (import soundfonts/samples BEFORE these presets)

Four presets reference a staged soundfont or sample by its **future content-hash UUID** — the same
`sha256(bytes) → UUID` scheme `scripts/import-soundfonts.mjs`/`scripts/import-samples.mjs` will
assign when that file is actually imported. Until that import happens, the UUID in the preset
resolves to nothing; **these four presets are inert placeholders until their asset is imported**,
same as any preset referencing a not-yet-imported sample/soundfont.

| Preset | References | Asset UUID | How it was computed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean Piano | `factory-staging/intake/soundfonts/GeneralUser-GS/GeneralUser-GS-v2.0.3.sf2` | `9575028c-7a1f-489f-9770-fccc8cff2734` | `sha256` of the raw `.sf2` bytes (soundfonts hash unconverted, per `import-soundfonts.mjs`). Independently recomputed and confirmed identical in this pass. |
| Orchestral Sketch (Harp) | `factory-staging/intake/soundfonts/FreePats-GM-Orchestral/FreePatsGM-20221026.sf2` | `f7bf84f9-2ae8-4b5f-9650-97e69aff7e4b` | Same, raw `.sf2` bytes. Independently recomputed and confirmed identical. |
| Guitar Cab Convolver | `factory-staging/intake/samples/Impulse-Responses/AdventureKid-AKRT-Speakers/ModernUk/AK-SPKRS_ModUk_001.wav` | `f51ed198-f47a-4253-b765-888e0c8d16e6` | `ffmpeg -ar 48000 -acodec pcm_f32le` conversion (exact args from `import-samples.mjs`'s `convert()`), then `sha256` of the converted bytes — samples hash the converted WAV, not the source file. Independently recomputed and confirmed identical. |
| Lo-Fi Sampler | `factory-staging/intake/samples/Keys/UIowaMIS-SteinwayPiano/Piano.mf.C4.aiff` | `0ab1a85f-1d07-4a24-8418-ab5a6b6e3490` | Same ffmpeg conversion + hash. Note: this source file is a ~31-second sustained note recording (long natural decay), not a trimmed one-shot — used as-is; whoever imports it later may want to trim it first. |

These asset UUIDs are independent of preset UUIDs (which regenerate on every run) and were
recomputed by literally running the real hashing (and, for samples, the real ffmpeg conversion)
against the staged files — not guessed. Import order matters: run
`import-soundfonts.mjs`/`import-samples.mjs` on these specific files before (or with) this preset
batch, or the four presets above will silently point at nothing in the running instance.

The other five presets (Drum Bus, Vocal Chain, Mastering Chain, Ambient Send, Synth Bass) reference
no external assets and work immediately, independent of import order.

## Skipped / scoped down

- **Sidechain-style pump — skipped entirely.** `CompressorDeviceBox` and `GateDeviceBox` both do
  expose a real `side-chain` pointer field (`Pointers.SideChain`), and `AudioUnitBox`/`AudioBusBox`
  both accept incoming `SideChain` pointers — the DSP support genuinely exists. But the side-chain
  source has to be a *second* track or bus in the project, routed in as a trigger signal. A
  self-contained effect-chain preset — built the same way `PresetEncoder.encodeEffects` builds one,
  around a single synthetic wrapper audio unit — has no second track to route from; there's nothing
  in that shape for the side-chain pointer to legitimately target. Approximating the "pump" with
  just a fast-attack/fast-release compressor would misrepresent what the preset actually does (it
  wouldn't duck against anything), so this was left out rather than faked.
- **Orchestral sketch — scoped down to a single instrument, not skipped.** The brief already flagged
  this one as not fitting the single-preset model (it's more a multi-instrument idea). Scoped down
  to "Orchestral Sketch (Harp)": a single `SoundfontDeviceBox` preset pointed at FreePats GM
  Orchestral's Orchestral Harp patch. Worth noting honestly: despite its name, that soundfont's
  orchestral coverage is thin — it has no real strings or brass, only synth-substitute patches
  sitting at those GM program numbers ("Synth Strings 1/2", "Synth Brass 1/2"). Orchestral Harp and
  Timpani are the only two genuinely orchestral instruments it contains; Harp was picked as the more
  melodically usable of the two.
- **Vocal Chain's reverb — left out, not faked as a series effect.** The brief allowed "optionally a
  reverb send." A true send is bus/mixer-level routing (a separate aux bus the chain sends to in
  parallel), which a single linear effect-chain preset can't express — inserting a reverb device in
  series at the end of the chain would be a different, wetter effect than a send, not an honest
  stand-in for one. Vocal Chain ships as Gate → Revamp (EQ) → Compressor only.

## Verification performed

- Built with the **real, compiled `@opendaw/studio-boxes` device classes** (generated by the real
  `box-forge` codegen from `packages/studio/forge-boxes/src/schema/**`) and the real
  `ProjectSkeleton` / `AudioUnitFactory` / `PresetEncoder` from `@opendaw/studio-adapters` — not a
  reimplementation. All 9 presets built with zero errors.
- Every `.odp` file was **round-tripped through the real `PresetDecoder`**: instrument/rack presets
  via `PresetDecoder.decode` into a fresh `ProjectSkeleton`, chain presets via
  `PresetDecoder.insertEffectChain` onto a fresh audio unit's `audioEffects` field — the identical
  calls `PresetEncoder.composite.test.ts`'s passing vitest suite makes. Every decode succeeded with
  no failed/dangling mandatory pointers.
- For the 3 asset-referencing presets, the decoded box graph's `Convolver.file` /
  `Soundfont.file` pointer was walked to its target box and confirmed to be a real
  `AudioFileBox`/`SoundfontFileBox` carrying the expected precomputed UUID and file name (not just
  "a pointer exists" — the actual referenced box and its identity were checked).
- `index.json` parses as a JSON array of 9 objects, each matching the real `PresetMeta` shape
  (`packages/studio/core/src/presets/PresetMeta.ts`): `uuid`, `name`, `description`, `created`,
  `modified`, `category`, plus `device` (instrument/audio-effect/midi-effect presets) or
  `instrument` (audio-unit/rack presets) where the type requires it.
- The soundfont `preset-index` values were independently reconfirmed against the real `soundfont2`
  library (same one the engine uses) rather than trusted from the prior draft.
